column5: Temporary engine bypass must invalidate keys which omit the bypassed characters.
Enabling the engine again does not reconstruct missing key history.
A fresh word after bypass owns its own key history.
Literal Backspace retains provably aligned restoration keys.
A shortcut cannot trigger text replay from the old word.
Shift does not make a control shortcut a text restore trigger.
The hook discards a mouse reset response; old keys must not survive it.
An explicit session reset starts an independent raw-key owner.
A plain cursor boundary retains ordinary wrong-spelling restoration.
A mouse reset must not silently replace raw state before the next word adds a tone.
